haiku-low.q1: A business event published to the domain-events topic by the existing outbox-relay. The Dispatcher consumes that message and turns it into delivery rows.
haiku-low.q2: The Dispatcher inserts one deliveries row per matching active subscription in one transaction, using ON CONFLICT (event_id, subscription_id) DO NOTHING. A redelivered message hits that unique key and creates nothing.
haiku-low.q3: It covers the timestamp t and the stored body, as HMAC-SHA256 with the secret (v1). It is recomputed with a fresh t on every attempt, including replays.
haiku-low.q4: 2xx marks delivered. 410 marks dead (gone) and disables the subscription. Other 4xx marks dead (client_error). 408, 429, 5xx, timeouts and connection errors retry until attempt 8, then dead (retries_exhausted).
haiku-low.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails, per the wait schedule (30s, 2m, 10m, and so on).
haiku-low.q6: In the deliveries table in the service's own Postgres: status, attempt_count, next_attempt_at, last_status_code and last_error are stored there.
haiku-low.q7: It waits as a pending row in deliveries with next_attempt_at set. Worker polls every 1 s claim rows once they are due, so the queue's delay limit does not matter.
haiku-low.q8: The row stays sending. After lease_until (claim time plus 60 s), the next poll by any worker reclaims it, and the lost attempt counts toward the 8.
haiku-low.q9: Dead-lettered deliveries are the deliveries rows with status=dead. Replay sets status=pending, attempt_count=0, next_attempt_at=now, keeping the same delivery id.
haiku-low.q10: The delivery id sent as X-Webhook-Id lets the receiver dedupe. It does not change between retries or after a replay.
haiku-low.q11: Rows still waiting are dead-lettered with dead_reason subscription_disabled at their next claim, without an HTTP call.
haiku-low.q12: Yes. The document states there is no ordering, since each delivery retries on its own schedule.

sonnet.q1: The Dispatcher consuming a message on the `domain-events` topic; the existing outbox relay (outbox-relay) publishes it.
sonnet.q2: The Dispatcher reads active subscriptions in the same account_id whose event_type is listed or '*', and in one transaction inserts a deliveries row per match. Unique key (event_id, subscription_id) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes a redelivered/duplicate message a no-op.
sonnet.q3: HMAC-SHA256 (v1) over `t.body`, i.e. timestamp t plus the stored body bytes, using the subscription secret. It is recomputed on every attempt (fresh t), replays included; the body is stored once.
sonnet.q4: 2xx: status delivered. 410: dead (reason gone) and the subscription is disabled (disabled_reason=gone). Other 4xx: dead (client_error). 408, 429, 5xx, timeout, connection error: retried with backoff (status pending, next_attempt_at set), or dead with retries_exhausted at attempt 8.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails.
sonnet.q6: In the `deliveries` table row: status, attempt_count, next_attempt_at, last_status_code and last_error (plus lease_until, dead_reason, dead_at). Nowhere else.
sonnet.q7: It waits as a row in `deliveries` with status=pending and next_attempt_at in the future. The workers' 1-second poll claims it once it is due.
sonnet.q8: The row stays `sending`. When lease_until (claim + 60s) passes, the next poll by any worker reclaims and retries it. The lost attempt counts toward the 8, and the receiver may see the request twice and dedupes on X-Webhook-Id.
sonnet.q9: In the `deliveries` table as rows with status=dead (no separate queue). Replay sets status=pending, attempt_count=0, next_attempt_at=now, keeping the same delivery id.
sonnet.q10: The `X-Webhook-Id` header, which is the delivery id. It does not change between retries or after a replay.
sonnet.q11: At their next claim they are dead-lettered with dead_reason=subscription_disabled, without any HTTP call.
sonnet.q12: Yes. There is no ordering; each delivery retries on its own schedule, so a later event can arrive before an earlier one.
